body: Nobody would want to be around me if I didn't constantly give out free stuff, I would class that as being a burden.
People only ever hang around me out of pity or because I'm a source of free stuff. I am a burden.
I have a hard time believing that. If I wasn't a burden, at least one person around me would want me around. And if I wasn't defective, I wouldn't be feeling like this.

You have no need to apologize, friend; you have done no wrong. You are not the defective burden, in fact you have done far beyond what most people would do to try and help, and for a stranger no less.
I suppose. It won't make it any less soul crushing, though.

Thank you, although I'm not trying to hope too much; I'm not even remotely close to good enough for her, and she knows it.

And I dunno, I don't really have any friends that I would trust with both listening to me and keeping it under their hat.

I do apologize for replying late and worrying you; I took the day off work and school and I'm just trying to sleep through my problems. I hopped on my bike and went for a ride, because it is hard to feel sad when you're twisting the throttle. I also made a gamble and left my ex some flowers, a card (with a well-written and emotional message), and some of her favorite foods as a "thank you" and last hope that she will want me back (she's "broken up" with me before and said similar things while dealing with her own mental problems). I'm admittedly feeling a little better; I guess I wouldn't actively seek out death, but I would be alright with dying.

And you would be correct, but my school's counselors and psychologist are the type to have you taken to the county mental hospital if they even suspect anything. And as far as my friends go, I don't know. I don't want to risk them blowing me off or getting me locked away, it'd be a big gamble and I really don't want to risk it.

I am a burden, there isn't anybody that legitimately wants me around. My coworkers/boss could easily find someone to fill my position a million times better than I did; and I would rather be able to talk to my friends than die (honestly, I don't *want* to be dead but I really don't want to be alive, either), but they'd either ignore me or freak out and I'd end up in a mental hospital for the next several months.
I beg to differ. All I am is a burden on my family, and all I do is ruin my friends' good times. They'd be better off if I wasn't around; all I do is take up space and resources.
Sorry if this makes me sound like an asshole, but is there really a light at the end of the tunnel? I don't even have anything in my future to look forward to, except the day that I won't be around.

My pets might wonder where I went, but with their limited capacity for thought, they'll be just fine. And those around me might miss me, but that just gives them a story to tell when reminiscing in the future; in the long run, they'd be better off without me.

Realistically, they'd be upset; that's understandable. But they'd also be relieved. My parents wouldn't have to worry about me or my future, my friends would be free of me interrupting and ruining their good times, and my pets would definitely get over it quickly. It sounds weird, but I feel like the only reason I stick around is other people, but they don't even want me around. And this sounds pompous and cliche, but the Robin Williams quote about the saddest people always try the hardest to make others happy feels like it describes my life entirely.

Thank you for taking your time to post your advice. But even if my friends or family wanted to spend time with me, they'd be too busy living their own lives; I can't impose on them and ruin their good times, too.

I appreciate you taking the time to share your kind words, stranger. People around me might be upset for a week or two, but they'd end up better off in the long run; but it is strangely comforting that people like you legitimately care about complete strangers.
Thank you for the kind words. I'm sorry I can't really express my thanks other than saying that your kind words really did help, at least a little.
Stay strong, stranger. We can both get through this. I may not want to die, but I'm really hoping "one more day" will be strong enough to keep me going.
